# Awesome Reliability Tools

A curated, actively maintained directory of tools for the service reliability lifecycle:

**Detect → Respond → Communicate**

- **Detect**: uptime / availability monitoring
- **Respond**: incident management and on-call coordination
- **Communicate**: status pages and subscriber notifications

This list is built from a [structured dataset](data/tools.yaml). The README, comparison tables, generated JSON, and the [website](https://dragstor.github.io/awesome-reliability-tools/) are all generated from that dataset.

## Why this exists

Reliability tooling is spread across several overlapping awesome lists, most of which stopped being maintained years ago. This project keeps a single, neutral, verification-first directory for the whole reliability lifecycle and makes every claim traceable to a primary source.

It is not a ranking. There are no scores, "best" labels, or paid placements. Tools owned by the maintainers of this project follow exactly the same rules as every other entry.

**Maintainer disclosure:** This project is maintained by the founder of [StatusPage.me](https://statuspage.me/). StatusPage.me is included and documented using the same criteria, evidence requirements, sorting, and presentation as every other tool. It receives no featured placement or preferential treatment.

## Feature-state legend

| Icon | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| Yes | Supported |
| No | Unsupported |
| ? | Unknown / unverified |
| — | Not applicable |

A claim marked **Unknown / unverified** does not mean unsupported. It means we have not yet confirmed the capability from a primary source. **Not applicable** means the capability is outside the scope of what the tool does, based on its declared categories.

## Verification model

- Every capability is stored as one of the four states above.
- A **supported** or **unsupported** claim must carry at least one primary source URL and a `verified_at` date.
- Absent claims inside a tool's own categories are treated as **unknown**, not unsupported.
- Claims outside a tool's declared categories are treated as **not applicable**.
- Archived and deprecated tools are retained and labelled so the history is not lost.

See [METHODOLOGY.md](METHODOLOGY.md) for the full rules.

## Methodology and contribution

- [METHODOLOGY.md](METHODOLOGY.md) explains how entries are selected, verified, and kept neutral.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) describes the pull-request workflow for adding or updating a tool.
- Corrections from vendors and users are welcome through the same PR process.
